slides.title: When a school closes, what happens to its students?
slides.body: I followed twenty years of Ministry of Education records to find out.

slides.title: A map shows buildings, not the children who have to move.
slides.body: When a school closes, it often seems enough that another school is nearby. But that says nothing about whether its students kept studying or moved up a grade the next year.

slides.title: I followed every student, year by year

stats.label: similar students from schools that stayed open, for comparison

slides.note: Each student was compared with others of the same year, age, grade, sex, region and type of school.

slides.kicker: The first thing that shows up
slides.title: 19 out of 19 years, the same direction
slides.body: Each bar is one year: how many more students, per hundred, fell behind a grade or stopped appearing as enrolled the next year, compared with their peers.
slides.note: Some years have few cases and a lot of uncertainty. That is why looking at all of them together matters.

slides.body: For every hundred students who lost their school, about 6 more than among their peers fell behind or left the register the next year.
slides.note: Average across all years: +6.29 percentage points (between +4.49 and +8.09). For a new round of closures, the expected range is +0.09 to +12.49.

slides.title: The gap kept shrinking
slides.subtitle: Additional students per hundred, average for each period.
slides.note: I cannot credit any one policy: the schools that close also changed, as did the way records are kept and, during the pandemic, the rules for moving up a grade.

slides.title: I cannot yet say the closure is the cause
slides.body: The schools that closed were already more fragile, with less full-day schooling and fewer support agreements. And many of their students were already switching schools:
slides.note: Had already switched schools at least once in the previous two years (2016–2019 window).

slides.title: If more closures are coming, look first at where they will happen
slides.body: The demographic transition may bring new closures and mergers. Knowing where they will happen makes it possible to plan in time:
items: Real vacancies and safe transport to the new school
Support for the school that receives the students
Guidance for students and families through the change
Tracking every student for at least two years
